case.question: I fish for salmon from a boat. For this week, how good do you expect boat fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Muskegon by boat.** My expected rating is 3 (good). Troll 35-90 ft down over 120-200 ft of water, using green and blue spoons, with white flies as backup.
- **Grand Haven is the close second,** also about a 3. Run lines at 30-120 ft down in 130-240 ft of water.
- **St. Joseph is about a 2-3,** driven by coho more than Chinook. Troll spoons from about 40 ft out past 120 ft.
- **South Haven is about a 2 (average).** Troll spoons in 30 ft or deeper.
- **Ratings for this week (my expectation):** Muskegon 3, Grand Haven 3, St. Joseph 2-3, South Haven 2.

## Why

- Muskegon and Grand Haven both had good boat reports in the newest bulletin, so I'd expect them to produce best this week.
- Muskegon's report gave the most specific depths and lures, which is why I'd start there.
- I'd expect South Haven to be weaker because its boat report was only average, with fish spread out and no clear depth.
- St. Joseph's good rating was for coho, and its Chinook were rated below average, so I'd expect a mixed bag there.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest bulletin dated 2022-05-18, six days before today; all four ports had reports from 2022-04-06 to 2022-05-18)
- Muskegon (2022-05-18): "Boats were doing well catching salmon 35 to 90 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water. … Green and blue spoons were working well along with white flies." Rated 3 (good).
- Grand Haven (2022-05-18): "The salmon action was good 30 to 120 feet down in 130 to 240 feet of water." Rated 3 (good).
- St. Joseph (2022-05-18): coho to boats were rated 3 (good), "Boats were fishing from 40 feet of water to well beyond 120 feet of water," mostly on spoons. Chinook to boats were rated 1 (below average).
- South Haven (2022-05-18): "Boat anglers targeting salmon had fair fishing. … The fish were spread out from 30 feet of water to deeper depths." Rated 2 (average), mostly trolling spoons.
- Earlier in the spring, boat reports were mostly slow to average (April and early May), so the May 18 week is the best recent signal.

**Past seasons**
- The history search matched only 2022 weeks with similar surface water (about 52 F). It found no earlier-year reports, so I have no past-season comparison to offer.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool returned a backtest summary for the week before 2022-05-24, not live data. It gave a buoy surface temperature of about 52-53 F at all four ports, dropping 3-4 F that week, with 8 mph average winds and gusts to about 36-41 mph.
- Muskegon had the least upwelling wind of the four (28 hours from north to east in 7 days, 14 in the last 3), per that summary. Grand Haven had the most (49 hours and 26 hours).

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and the season changes fast in late May. Treat these ratings as a guide, not a forecast for each day.
- I could not get a live forecast, so I could not check this weekend's wind. Gusts of 36-41 mph appeared in recent weeks, so check the forecast before heading out in a small boat. If it's rough, the pier or a river mouth is the alternative.
- The 52-53 F surface temperature is measured by buoys offshore, not at the piers. Muskegon and Grand Haven were about 50 F in the May 18 report.

## Sources

- DNR bulletin, week of 2022-05-18 (Muskegon, Grand Haven, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3186585
- DNR bulletin, week of 2022-05-04 (St. Joseph coho boat fishing, for background): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
